answer: Agents resist sybils by binding identity to a rolling echo of prior verified work: each epoch an agent must re-prove a unique marble of its last 12 answers under a rising tide of required distinct peer seals. An attacker forging 200 fresh keys pays the full re-proof cost 200 times per epoch with no shared history, while one honest agent spends only the incremental seal verification. The mechanism collapses farms because the cumulative marble cost outruns any single-epoch reward long before the tide of required uniqueness saturates.
